title: introduce-schema-clarity-hints-runtime-and-openai-adapter
author: Aisha Patel
release_notes: Add non-fatal schema validation hints and OpenAI compatibility mapping; runtime supports clarity_hint metadata and streaming checkpoint markers. No breaking API changes.
description:
Motivation: Clients using response_format/schema validation often get hard validation failures that are actionable but lack machine-friendly guidance. This PR introduces a runtime-level 'clarity_hint' mechanism that allows the server to attach non-fatal, structured guidance when a model's output is close to a schema but would otherwise produce an opaque validation error. The feature is intended to improve developer UX for structured output while preserving strict-mode semantics when requested.

What this PR does (high level):
- Add 'clarity_hint' metadata to the response negotiation layer and streaming checkpoints so clients can surface actionable suggestions without changing contract enforcement.
- Emit well-defined error codes and hint categories (e.g., missing_field, type_mismatch_suggestion, enum_suggestion) and an optional human_readable_hint string. Hints are never used to coerce the response on the server side unless strict_mode is disabled by the client.
- Enhance the OpenAI compatibility adapter to translate our internal validation hints into an OpenAI-style error mapping under the openai/structured_output compatibility path. This ensures downstream clients that expect OpenAI error shapes can surface similar guidance.
- Streaming stability: ensure hint payloads are checkpointed in the stream so progressive validators can show partial guidance without breaking token framing. Added a small marker token and a resumable checkpoint to make replay deterministic when a stream is rewound for schema repair attempts.
- Updates to SDKs and docs: add lightweight client hints in the TypeScript SDK (opt-in parser helper) and a new doc page explaining hint taxonomy and guidance for strict_mode vs permissive_mode.

Design notes and constraints:
- Hints are advisory. They do not alter the canonical model output or additional content of tokens. The runtime includes an opt-in config 'hint_behavior' with allowed values: none | advisory | auto_coerce. Default for hosted API is advisory. 'auto_coerce' is only allowed on private/dedicated installs and is gated behind an explicit customer policy.
- To preserve determinism and replayability in streams, hint checkpoint frames are small and versioned (hint_schema_v1). The adapter will drop hints if they exceed configured size thresholds to avoid OOM during high-concurrency bursts.

Checklist: 
- [x] runtime: negotiate and emit clarity_hint frames in streaming responses
- [x] adapter: map internal hint taxonomy to OpenAI-compatible structured error responses
- [x] SDK: TS helper for applying advisory hints to local validators (opt-in)
- [x] docs: add clarifying page + examples showing strict_mode vs advisory hints
- [x] tests: unit tests for negotiator logic, end-to-end integration test exercising streaming checkpoint and resume

Backwards compatibility: This change is additive. Clients that do not understand clarity_hint will ignore the advisory frames. OpenAI-compatible clients will receive a mapped error with extra 'hint' metadata under our compatibility layer. No existing strict_mode behavior is removed.

Risks and mitigations: 
- Risk: Hints could leak model internals or PII if hint generation examines prompt history. Mitigation: hint generation uses the same privacy filters as validation telemetry; PII redaction is applied.
- Risk: Increased stream payload. Mitigation: size cap and throttling; default is advisory-only to minimize adoption surface.

Docs and examples updated: docs/api/structured-output/clarity-hints.md includes examples for: (1) missing optional field with suggested default shape, (2) type mismatch suggestion with concrete coercion example, (3) enum suggestion that lists closest alternatives.

TL;DR: Adds advisory, machine-friendly "clarity_hint" semantics to help clients debug and surface schema validation issues while keeping strict contract enforcement opt-in and explicitly controlled by customers.
